A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PhysGen and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Corresponding content can be matched reliably, including the replaced generalization experiment and expanded appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original shape-generation, reconstruction, aerodynamic-estimation, ablation, and CFD results, including Tables 1–8 and supplementary Table A.

after.justification: v2 retains original vehicle experiments and adds reconstruction comparisons and structural-optimization results in Table 4, Figure 8, and supplementary Figure C.

M1.justification: The aerodynamic SP-VAE architecture, losses, and alternating generation algorithm remain unchanged. Appendix G adds a structural adaptation using differentiable FEM and compliance minimization, with one velocity update after every five physical-refinement steps. This changes the procedure for the new application without redesigning the core framework.

E1.justification: v1's BlendedNet aircraft pressure-prediction experiment is removed. v2 instead evaluates structural optimization of load-bearing objects under prescribed forces and boundary conditions, including furniture, a figurine, and a lamp. This substantially changes the physical domain and task coverage; DrivAerNet++ and ShapeNet vehicle experiments remain.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds the VAEs of Hunyuan3D 2.1 and Hi3DGen to the reconstruction comparison. Figure 8 introduces structural comparisons against Hunyuan3D 2.1 initial shapes and PhysiOpt, substantially broadening evaluated comparators. Table 1's SP-VAE+TripOptimizer label clarifies a reproduction using SP-VAE; its unchanged scores do not establish a different experiment.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces a structural protocol reporting compliance and mean displacement, with 180 optimization steps for both PhysiOpt and PhysGen and a specified interleaving schedule. Existing vehicle splits, training epochs, sampling settings, and OpenFOAM procedures remain unchanged. The protocol additions are confined to the new structural evaluation.

E4.justification: The aircraft transfer analysis is replaced by structural case studies examining load-induced deformation and optimization artifacts in Figures 8 and C. The training-strategy, decoder-component, alternating-update, and drag-versus-pressure analyses remain unchanged, so the revision affects a limited portion of the supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain Table A's averages over 20 samples per dataset. The new mean-displacement metric is not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial new results: Table 4 reports overall accuracy/IoU of 89.43/76.55 for Hunyuan3D 2.1 and 91.47/81.52 for Hi3DGen. Structural Figure 8 reports PhysGen compliance of 0.32 and 1.08 versus PhysiOpt's 0.74 and 2.89, with four further cases in Figure C. Aircraft pressure results are removed. Existing vehicle benchmark values remain unchanged; these additions are not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix G adds the structural formulation K(z)u = f and the compliance objective C = f^T u, introducing a linear-static equilibrium model for the new application. Existing flow-matching and aerodynamic mathematics remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces airplane-design generalization with structural optimization, and the conclusion now explicitly claims generalization to that task. The central contributions—SP-VAE, physics-regularized flow matching, and alternating refinement—retain their original meaning.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation of structural failures: thin supports deform under load, while physics-only optimization introduces geometric artifacts that shape-prior updates mitigate. Section 4.2 also qualifies the TripOptimizer comparison as a reproduced two-stage strategy. The former aircraft-transfer interpretation is removed; other mechanism explanations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-and-weights repository pointer, discloses the SP-VAE implementation of the TripOptimizer comparison, and documents the structural FEM procedure. Appendix A changes reported GPUs from A100 to H100 and pressure/joint-training times from 22/18 to 21/15 hours, without establishing reruns. The presentation.mp4 pointer is removed. Most existing implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hunyuan3D 2.1 and Hi3DGen references, removes BlendedNet, and replaces the text-to-SQL survey citation with a general large-language-model survey. PhysiOpt, already cited in v1, gains a substantive role as a structural comparator. The main related-work framing remains stable; publication and bibliographic updates are not new works.

P1.justification: Changes include local rewrites of the comparison discussion and conclusion, new Section 4.5 and Appendix G, revised algorithm comments, and author/contact/acknowledgement edits. Most prose and the overall section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 8 replaces aircraft pressure plots with structural comparisons, and Figure C adds structural examples. Table 4 expands and moves into a single-column layout; Table 7 gains units. Architecture diagrams, legends, and captions receive localized revisions, while most existing visual evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves comparison transparency by identifying the SP-VAE-based TripOptimizer reproduction, adds relevant reconstruction baselines, and supplies code/weights access information. Its structural examples test the framework beyond aerodynamics, but replace aircraft-transfer evidence and remain illustrative case studies. These are useful, limited gains; the core vehicle results and method are largely unchanged.
